lessons: Legal-gate hardening applied: a negative eligibility statement needs a named route back (BVA or a lawyer) when the official leaflet omits the rule, because a reader can act on a negative without ever checking it.
Resolved this cycle (were deferred in 2.2.0): the Anschluss-Austrian exclusion from the German routes, and the Vienna Heimatrecht point.

The Anschluss exclusion is 'grundsätzlich', with narrow carve-outs (German before 1938 or by descent; Austria did not reclaim the person under the 1925 Act loss grounds). The skill states the rule and names the exceptions without trying to adjudicate them.
The BVA's applicant-facing Merkblatt does not mention the Austria exclusion at all; it lives in the BMI Anwendungshinweise and the case law. Re-check when the BVA leaflet is next revised.
Still deferred: Germany §14 discretionary naturalization; Poland marriage and mother-line rules; minors; Lithuania; digital apostille; Hungary language re-check; Czech exclusions.

Israel: digital apostille via the Ministry of Justice notaries authority for digitally signed certificates; a printout of a digitally signed PIBA certificate is not an original (State Comptroller Feb 2026). Add one sentence once a gov.il snippet is captured.

Coverage MAJOR deferred (unverified against primary sources, word cap 4986/5000): born-in-Vienna is not Austrian citizenship (Heimatrecht, post-1918 Polish citizenship of Galician Jews); Germany §14 StAG discretionary naturalization from abroad; Poland marriage-to-foreigner and illegitimate-child mother-line rules (1920 Act); minors applying; Lithuania after the failed 2024 referendum.
